newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Conference organiser freed by Mauritius police.
newsitem.headline: Conference organiser freed by Mauritius police.

text.p: The organiser of a major oil and minerals conference in Mauritius who was arrested at the weekend on fraud charges was set free on Tuesday.

"I don't know what's happening to me, I have just arrived from (a) police cell, please understand," said Humphrey Harrison, managing director of Europe Energy Environment which organised the three-day conference at Grand Baie.
Harrison said he would be staying for a few more days in the Indian Ocean island to sort out outstanding issues.

Harrison's wife Karin told Reuters in South Africa that Mauritius government officials and hotel staff refused to accept payment for outstanding conference bills through bank transfer and insisted on cash.

"On Saturday afternoon my husband and myself were arrested," she said. She was released later in the day after pleading with police to let her return to her Johannesburg home to attend to her three young children. She paid a portion of the bill on her personal credit card.

Her husband appeared in court on Monday on charges of conspiring to fraudently obtain credit, and the case was postponed to June 30. She said payment of around 30,000 pounds -- mainly for catering costs -- was made by bank transfer to the hotel on Monday.
"There was no problem in transferring the money, the money has been paid," Harrison said.

But a police officer in Port Louis said: "This morning, a bank confirmed a transfer of about 1.0 million rupees, representing 75 percent of the bill in favour of Le Mauricia Hotel. We are trying to negotiate to have the rest, but I think that he will pay it under protest."
Harrison declined to comment on the charges.
On Monday, Harrisson was charged and refused bail. Police said they opposed the bail application until a large proportion of money owed to the hotel arrived on Tuesday.
The conference is a showcase for sub-Saharan oil and mining with several African ministers attending. It was held for the fourth time this year.
